focus: Autonomous trucking clears a regulatory milestone, voice AI confronts its accuracy gap, and Nadella calls for architectural containment of AI models.

headlines.title: FMCSA grants autonomous trucks a five-year warning-device exemption
headlines.body: The US Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration gave Aurora and other Level 4 carriers a five-year exemption to replace roadside reflective triangles with cab-mounted amber beacons. The ruling, signed October 7, covers Kodiak AI, Waabi and Stack AV and is backed by 500,000-plus miles of test data with zero beacon faults. It replaces four rolling three-month waivers Aurora had held since October 2025.

headlines.title: Kodiak AI and Charger launch 435-mile Dallas–Laredo autonomous trucking lane
headlines.body: Kodiak’s Driver-as-a-Service platform began hauling refrigerated and dry freight for Charger Logistics between Dallas and the highest-volume US–Mexico land port. A safety driver remains for now; Kodiak’s Autonomy Readiness Measure hit 96% in September and the company targets driverless service on I-45 by year-end.

headlines.title: Voice AI execs say the sector hasn’t reached its ChatGPT moment
headlines.body: PolyAI’s CTO and other voice-agent leaders told TechCrunch that full-duplex models, ASR accuracy and transparency remain unsolved. Latency, hallucinated responses and a lack of user trust are blocking mass adoption in enterprise call centers despite rapid investment.

headlines.title: XPENG names robotaxi service YOYO and opens public sign-ups
headlines.body: The Chinese EV maker branded its Level 4 ride-hailing business XPENG YOYO and began inviting the public to trial rides in Guangzhou. The platform runs a camera-only VLA 2.0 model on four in-house Turing chips delivering 3,000 TOPS, with no LiDAR or HD maps. Over 2,000 internal test rides preceded the public launch.

headlines.title: Boston Dynamics reveals mass-manufacturing humanoid hand
headlines.body: A redesigned four-finger, 13-DOF hand built from 13 identical fully encapsulated actuators with no cables crossing joints. It handles loads over 100 lb and was designed for high-fidelity sim-to-real reinforcement learning. The hand is in use at headquarters but not yet deployed across the full Atlas fleet.

headlines.title: Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
headlines.body: Microsoft’s CEO argued for separating models from their orchestration harnesses, externalizing controls, logging every meaningful action with tamper-proof evidence, and giving authorized humans a kill switch. ‘Assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,’ he wrote, aligning with Amodei’s September call for pacing the frontier.

headlines.title: Avride and Sodexo Campus to scale delivery robots across ~425 US colleges
headlines.body: The autonomous mobility company and Sodexo Campus signed a framework agreement to accelerate sidewalk robot deployments from months to weeks across Sodexo’s 425-institution US network. Avride has completed over 600,000 autonomous deliveries and currently operates at Ohio State, Indiana, Arizona and Salisbury.

headlines.title: Helm.ai signs $70M in commercial contracts for autonomous perception
headlines.body: The Redwood City startup reported $70M in signed contracts over 12 months for its deep-teaching foundation models, which span Level 2 through Level 4 autonomy and extend to mining, construction and drones. CEO Vladislav Voroninski says the company is now tracking toward operational breakeven.

headlines.title: Vocca raises $20M for voice AI medical receptionists
headlines.body: Norrsken VC led the Series A with Heal Capital, Speedinvest and Firstminute. The Paris-and-New-York startup handles over 1 million patient interactions a month across 20-plus specialties, with 70% resolved end-to-end without humans. Practitioners on the platform grew from 2,000 to 15,000 in a year.

trends.title: Autonomous trucking regulation catches up with deployment
trends.body: FMCSA’s first five-year exemption replaces rolling waivers, and Kodiak’s 96% safety-case readiness suggests driverless long-haul freight on US highways by year-end.

trends.title: Camera-only AV stacks go mainstream
trends.body: XPENG YOYO’s VLA 2.0 approach drops LiDAR and HD maps entirely. As compute costs fall and vision-language models improve, more OEMs may follow Tesla’s lead.

trends.title: Voice AI confronts its accuracy reckoning
trends.body: PolyAI’s CTO says full-duplex models and ASR still aren’t reliable enough for enterprise. Vocca’s 70% automation ceiling, impressive for healthcare, underscores the gap.

trends.title: Humanoid hardware pivots to mass-manufacturing design
trends.body: Boston Dynamics’ identical-actuator, cable-free hand prioritizes production scalability and sim-to-real transfer over raw dexterity, signaling readiness for fleet-scale deployment.

trends.title: AI safety moves from abstract principles to containment architecture
trends.body: Nadella’s proposal for external controls, tamper-proof logging and human kill switches follows Amodei’s pacing call. The framing has shifted from ‘should we slow down’ to ‘how do we build the brake.’
